correctness.rationale: For a matrix singular Herglotz field, entrywise nontangential limits are Hermitian a.e. since the representing positive measure is singular. The analytic inverse (H(z)-wI)^(-1) is bounded for Im w<0, and its angular mean is exactly (B+iT-wI)^(-1). Matrix-valued spectral integration produces a finite positive matrix measure with this resolvent. Entrywise Stieltjes inversion and -Im (B+iT-xI)^(-1) = (B-xI-iT)^(-1) T (B-xI+iT)^(-1) give the exact smooth positive density, with no atoms; strict T>0 guarantees invertibility and uniform real-axis regularity. Spectral calculus yields the half-positive projector and moment formulas. CHECK.py verifies four noncommuting 2x2 resolvent cases and 12 fractional moment quadratures; these finite checks supplement, not replace, the proof.

originality.rationale: The verified contemporary atomic theorem is scalar. The inspected older papers contain scalar Herglotz Cauchy laws, matrix Herglotz general machinery and a matrix spectral averaging identity in a different parameter. No inspected source states the explicit noncommuting operator-valued angular spectral measure for arbitrary positive singular matrix measures and arbitrary Hermitian drift. The claim is narrowly confined to this matrix boundary spectral law, not novelty of scalar Boole or general Herglotz inversion. Residual risk includes an equivalent under older matrix Herglotz spectral averaging terminology.
residual_risks: An uninspected operator-valued version of boundary distribution or spectral averaging may subsume the present formula, although none was identified in focused searches.
The full 1996 Poltoratski text was not materially examined; it must not be assumed to exclude extensions.
General matrix Herglotz tools make the proof relatively short; novelty is the explicit natural matrix spectral classification, not an invented new analytic lemma.

value.rationale: The noncommutative positive matrix field has no simultaneous eigenbasis and is not governed by scalar Boole substitution. The complete matrix-valued spectral measure, location-independent even for arbitrary singular-continuous matrix measures, is a natural sharp classification. Positive projector averaging, density depending only on B,T, and exact trace moment thresholds provide useful operator-valued harmonic-analysis invariants without claiming a downstream theorem.
